title: Exact results and JSON Pointer
summary: Use one RFC 6901 string JSON Pointer for exact nested addressing. resolvepointer powers bindings, readresult and completion checks.
html:
Exact results and JSON Pointer

Use one RFC 6901 string JSON Pointer for exact nested addressing. resolve_pointer powers bindings, read_result and completion checks.

{"input_bindings":[{"input_name":"patient_id","source_operation_id":"observed-operation-id","source_pointer":"/rows/0/patient_id"}]}

The engine passes the exact JSON value as inputs.patient_id, preserving strings, newlines, Unicode, empty strings, false, zero, null, arrays and objects. The model does not have to transcribe it. The receiving tool must declare input_bindings and inputs in its argument schema.

Pointer Meaning
empty string Whole result data
/stdout Top-level stdout
/response/user/id Nested object value
/rows/0/id First array item ID
/a~1b/~0key Keys a/b then ~key
/ Empty object key

Arrays require unsigned decimal indices without leading zeros. Missing keys, invalid escapes, out-of-range indices and traversal through scalars produce precise errors. Dotted paths, bracket syntax, URI fragments and fallback guessing are not supported.

With the execution.input_receipts check enabled, bindings reject missing, incomplete, explicitly unexecuted or failed source receipts. A complete, normally exited Shell/Python receipt is also eligible: its nonzero exit code is an observed result, not an automatic failure of the tool transport. Receipt-quality checks use the captured guard policy; disabling one does not grant access to another run. The result store always checks the caller's scope before returning exact data, including conversation-linked historical results. read_result can inspect an incomplete receipt for diagnosis. See bindings.py and completed_process_result.

Activity preflight receives the existing receipt store and a compact index combining historical and current results, with current records taking precedence. This authority stays local to preflight; it is not copied into Activity records or sent to a Gateway. Preflight leaves the proposed binding specification unchanged. Ordinary execution resolves it again against durable truth after admission, including resource or approval waits. A caller that omits the required authority gets input_binding_authority_unavailable rather than a Python lookup error.

Dependency graphs accept bindings to existing receipt operation IDs. Node names and Activity IDs are scheduling identities, not receipt aliases. The graph API does not provide future-value binding syntax: references to a new node or an unfinished Activity are rejected structurally before graph admission. Submit the consumer after the producer completes, using its receipt operation ID. Dependency-ready consumers revalidate existing bindings before execution; strict admission still checks the whole unstarted group and retains its existing conflict rules.

The Activity dependency guide shows the producer-to-consumer sequence and the separate role of prerequisite edges.

read_result with a pointer reads result data; omitting the pointer reads the receipt envelope. Its text is bounded JSON with offset/length information. Completion checks use {"operation_id":"observed-id","pointer":"/exit_code","equals":0}. Exact JSON types matter: false is not zero.

On historical input only, source_field="stdout" maps to /stdout; slash and tilde in old keys are escaped. It never guesses that dots in an old key meant nesting. See RFC 6901.

Recovering an omitted model view

Automatic results use the configured head/tail text allowance, shared across all streams in one response. The default is 6,000 characters from each end of the retained source. Execution status and exit code remain visible. The stored receipt stays intact, and explicit read pages keep their requested content and cursors.

An omitted-middle marker and truncated: true identify a shortened model view. source_complete: false identifies incomplete source coverage. Concrete recovery_actions give the exact tool, reference, pointer and offset to retrieve more. A receipt read cannot recover bytes absent from that receipt. For omitted backing-log output, the action names manage_job(action="logs", ...) with its job ID and byte cursor. Task Skill keeps its bounded historical excerpts and supplies the same preferred backing-log route where needed. These calls read existing evidence; the command does not need to run again.

{"reference":"observed-operation-id","pointer":"/stdout","offset":0,"limit":6000}

read_result offsets count characters of serialized JSON, including surrounding quotes and escaped newlines, not raw stdout characters or UTF-8 bytes. Its maximum page is 12,000 characters. Follow returned offsets; never guess an offset from a preview excerpt. Pointer "" selects receipt data; omitting the pointer selects the receipt envelope. References remain scoped across checkpoints and branches. Notebook references advertised alongside tool-result text previews use the same ownership-checked reader, even when Task Skill is not the carry-forward mode.

Automatic file list/find/search previews use the same text head/tail allowance and may split JSON records. Explicit result pages keep their existing record-aware paging and serialized-array offsets; oversized records use clearly labelled JSON fragments. Recover omitted records in the stored page before advancing the producer cursor to new source content. Explicit result pages bypass automatic preview shortening. The complete next model request still must fit its input budget; see the receipt-admission limitation below for the current error path when an alias page does not fit.

Availability, outcome and completeness

These fields answer different questions. A failed command can have a ready result whose diagnostic page is complete, even when the original output capture was partial.

Field Meaning
result_availability: pending An owned job or Activity is still active and final evidence is not available. The response supplies a wait action and has no final-result reference.
result_availability: blocked Recorded execution needs input or reconciliation; inspect its state. Unknown effects are not successful completion.
result_availability: unavailable Recorded evidence is missing, deleted or inaccessible. A guessed name does not recreate it.
result_availability: ready A readable result exists. This does not mean its execution succeeded or all source output was captured.
execution_outcome Captured cancellation/failure/success facts, independent of page size. Cancellation takes precedence; nonzero exit codes and explicit failure facts remain failures in this presentation.
Read-page complete This page reaches the end of the selected serialized value. A nonzero starting offset still omits earlier content.
source metadata Captured execution status, output completeness and retained byte extent, when recorded. Reading a complete page cannot repair missing original output.

result_availability.py resolves current-run operation, job and Activity identities through recorded links. A committed terminal receipt can take precedence over an older running row. An old predicted <job_id>_result name is considered only after finding an owned job; it does not create a receipt. Historical history/… references retain the notebook reader's frozen source and access checks. Launch receipts are never rewritten into terminal results. For groups, pending children take precedence over blocked and unavailable children; a ready child's own evidence remains independently readable. The final model projection can still carry a group's launch reference while its availability is pending. That field is not proof of a terminal result; use the availability and child facts. The retained mixed-group fixture expects the field to be absent and currently fails on this point, including at the starting revision of this documentation refresh.

Early reads and delivery

An accepted read_result that encounters pending execution becomes a subscription in canonical run state. It retains the original pointer, range and tool-call ID. The runtime suspends before another model decision and uses existing job/Activity supervision to wake it. It does not ask the model to repeatedly poll or relaunch work.

flowchart TD A[Accepted result read] --> R[Resolve owned execution] R -->|Ready| P[Read scoped receipt page] P --> T[Return correlated tool response] R -->|Pending| W[Register read and checkpoint] W --> S[Suspend run] S --> C[Existing supervisor or continuation wakes run] C --> U[Re-read the original scoped source] U -->|Still pending| S U -->|Page or terminal read error| D[Save correlated update and delivery marker] D --> M[Next accepted model decision consumes update] R -->|Blocked or unavailable| E[Return recorded state and recovery action]

result_waits.py saves the delivery marker together with the runtime completion message. Duplicate wakes do not append another page for that subscription. Retained updates survive ordinary history pruning and epoch changes until decision acceptance consumes them. Finish checks also cover accepted reads whose tool-call siblings have not joined yet, so a finish call cannot overtake a read in the same decision.

A user amendment can interrupt waiting for a progress reply; reply_and_resume_wait returns to the original wait if necessary. Explicit job detachment releases an existing subscription with an unavailable result and leaves the job running. Stopping the task clears its read obligation; clearing that obligation alone is not evidence of remote process cancellation. See jobs and scheduling for the separate execution-control owners.

Recovery and pinned pages

controls.py selects authorized receipt/notebook sources before JSON Pointer selection and paging. result_recovery.py pins an alias's returned continuation to its resolved historical receipt identity. If a later terminal receipt replaces the alias's current target, following the existing continuation still reads the originally selected receipt. Grants and deletion are rechecked on subsequent access.

An invalid pointer remains an error. The reader advertises actual available fields and may include one bounded, separately admitted recovery page. Recorded inputs use invocation read actions; output pointers start at receipt data. Neither a helpful recovery page nor readable historical evidence expands the eligibility of receipts used to validate task completion.

Receipt-admission limitation

The current generic receipt-alias budget-rejection path has a metadata mismatch. finish_page supplies a receipt-shaped candidate to context_reads.admit_result, whose rejection formatter requires attachment fields including context_id, source_bytes and sha256. An overflowing alias read can therefore raise KeyError: context_id instead of returning its intended smaller-page action. Ordinary attached-Context reads supply this metadata and return a structured budget error. Requesting a smaller explicit receipt page avoids requesting the same oversized page again; it does not require repeating execution.

The notebook recovery tests replace admission with a fixture callback, so their mocked rejection case does not establish that this real error branch works. This limitation was also reproduced at the documentation refresh's starting revision; the documentation changes leave its product behavior intact.

Implementation checks include test_result_wait_boundaries.py, test_result_waits.py, test_stored_output_recovery.py and test_file_observations.py.
